answer: Hardware-anchored admission: a credential needs an attestation quote signed by one physical chip's key, carrying this epoch's nonce. Checks stack like shale — chip certificate, nonce freshness, issuer registry; one missing layer rejects the key. The issuer enforces one active credential per device: no chip grazes the reward meadow twice, and cost doesn't ripple across clones — it repeats: each extra key needs its own hardware. Deterrence holds only while per-credential reward per epoch sits below amortized device cost per epoch; compromised chips or a bribed issuer break it.
